newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne rejects Invacare buyout offer.
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne rejects Invacare buyout offer.

text.p: Healthdyne Technologies Inc said its board of directors unanimously rejected an unsolicited acquisition offer from Invacare Corp.
"The board has not been and is not seeking to sell the company," said Craig Reynolds, Healthdyne chief executive.
In rejecting the offer, Healthdyne said its board considered several factors, "including the opinion of Cowen & Co that the $12.50 per share price offered by Invacare is grossly inadequate."

"Healthdyne Technologies is poised to introduce many new products in several markets during 1997 and in early 1998. These introductions will accelerate the shift toward more innovative, cost-effective and higher margin products. Due to competitive concerns, the release of detailed information on these products has been limited and therefore their importance to the company has not been fully appreciated by the investment community," Healthdyne said.
The company said it plans to release more information on the initiatives in early February with year-end results.

"Markets currently served by the company and those the company plans to enter are expected to grow from approximately $575 million in 1996 to approximately $1.2 billion in 1998," Reynolds said. "We have a history of successful product introductions, as most recently shown by the launch of Quantum, our non-invasive ventilator, which is expected to generate $12 million of revenue in its first full year."
Healthdyne, a medical devices maker, said it has also entered into key strategic sales and distribution agreements.
Invacare publicly unveiled its $12.50-per-share offer on January 10 and said the offer was first made on January 2.
On January 10, Invacare said its offer represented a 40-percent premium over Helthdyne's December 31 closing price.
On Thursday, Healthdyne closed at 13-1/2. At Friday's open, the shares moved down 1/8 to 13-3/8.
Healthdyne in October agreed to be exclusive distributor in U.S. and Canadian professional medical markets for the Breathe Right nasal strip made by CNS Inc.
Healthdyne reported third-quarter earnings of $1.2 million, flat over year-ago results, on revenues of $29.1 million versus $25.6 million a year earlier.

The Marietta, Ga.-based company's products include diagnostic and therapeutic devices for the evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders, non-invasive ventilators, oxygen concentrators and medication nebulizers for the treatment of respiratory disorders, monitors for infants at risk for sudden infant death syndrome and products for asthma management.
Invacare, based in Elyria, Ohio, makes respiratory products and mobility products for the disabled. Its shares were up 3/4 to 28 in early trading.
